decisions.summary: make task-start, make closing-checks and make decide take T=a,b,c as make land already does; a bundle gets one section and one verdict that counts for each task.
decisions.why: This is how the GM's 2026-11-22 request is carried out: bundle the open small tasks and work them at the same time, which he approved with 'so let's do that then'.

decisions.summary: active-task names the first member as task and every member as tasks. Each member's start is logged, the first member's last, so it is the task in force. All of a bundle's refusals are checked before anything is written.
decisions.why: This is how a bundle is started. A single task's flow is unchanged (Approach 1, 12).

decisions.summary: A member is refused when its box is not open, when it is a phase task (a parked stage's task included) or when its feature is held. The plan has no size test, so which tasks to bundle is the caller's choice.
decisions.why: The GM's words leave it to the session to look at the open tasks and pick the tiny ones, so leaving out a size test narrows nothing. A phase task is a stage of a staged plan, not one of the small defects the GM asked to bundle. A held feature or a closed box cannot be started alone either.

decisions.summary: Performance-first is checked for each member. A member that is not performance work is refused while an open performance task waits, unless that waiting task is a member of the same bundle. A performance task waiting outside the bundle still causes the refusal, with the same escape a single start has.
decisions.why: This is an exception to FR-013's literal start refusal. The GM's own words imply it: look at 'what set of tasks is currently open' and work them 'at the same time'. If the exception were refused, the performance member would have to go alone first, and every member would pay the fixed cost again, which is exactly what bundling exists to stop. It leaves FR-013's purpose intact, which is that performance work comes first and makes everything after it faster. The block says members are 'started, closed and landed together' and 'the landing ticks every member'. So a member that is not performance work can never land ahead of the performance member it shares a bundle with, and the end-to-end pin (land/tests/bundle.rs) lands the bundle as one unit. Counting each member as started for land-alone (T101) only lets the bundle land apart from other tasks. It does not let one member land apart from its own bundle. Any performance task outside the bundle still blocks as before.

decisions.id: D5 FR-006 bundle as the task
decisions.summary: One builder serves one bundle. The resume refusal after landing still fires because the landing ticks every member, whichever member's id the guard reads. The context-cap guard is unchanged.
decisions.why: This is an exception to FR-006's 'serves one task'. The GM's words call for it: working the tiny tasks 'at the same time' with one builder is how the builder's reading-in cost is paid once, and that cost is one of the fixed costs bundling exists to cut. FR-006's purpose is to keep builder contexts small, and that is still enforced without change. The context threshold guard is untouched, and resuming a builder after its bundle lands is still refused, since every member is ticked. This ruling does not rest on the members being small: a large bundle reaches the same context cap as a large task.

decisions.summary: The event log files a T=a,b,c command under the first member, so the static-runs guard and the plan-round tripwire count a bundle once. PLAN_ROUND_CAP and STATIC_RUNS_A_TASK are unchanged.
decisions.why: A bundle gets the same allowance one task gets, which is tighter than n tasks would get, not a carve-out from FR-007 or the round cap.

decisions.summary: make where-time reports a bundle's time under its first member (performance checklist 5). The other members carry no time of their own.
decisions.why: One builder's minute, one closing run and one review round in a bundle belong to the bundle, not to any one member. No per-member split could be true. The time is kept whole, so the categories (tests, compile, gate, land, review) and the totals the retrospective tooling exists to show are intact. This is a difference in how the time is reported, not a wrong answer from the tool.

decisions.summary: A heading that opens with a list of task ids followed by (bundle), Approach, part B or Performance checklist belongs to every listed task. Any other list heading still belongs to its first task, which keeps feature 405's 15 existing headings as they were. The search space is stated: a grep of specs/*/plan*.md.
decisions.why: The bundle section needs this, and the plan does not change how past plans are read.

decisions.summary: make decide T=a,b,c is refused while a member's section is not the first member's, or while T= differs from the heading's list, and the refusal names the fix. The lint runs once and the checklist once per member. One MODE 4 prompt asks the reviewer to judge every task in the bundle.
decisions.why: The bundle's single review, which the request implies.

decisions.id: D10 the verdict, tick and push
decisions.summary: record-task on the first member writes the same entry under each listed member that shares the section. owed_for and judge_in treat a block as in scope when any of the tasks sharing it is. The Approach gate and the plan-round count read the bundle heading for each member.
decisions.why: One verdict that counts for each member, as the bundle needs.

decisions.summary: The split in make closing-checks T=a,b,c takes a set of tasks, and the members' edit lines count as the caller's.
decisions.why: One set of closing runs per bundle, which is the fixed cost the GM asked to pay once.

decisions.summary: T141 is classed as performance work under FR-013 because it makes the builders' loop faster.
decisions.why: FR-013 defines performance work to include a task that makes the builders' loop faster, and the GM asked on 2026-11-20 for performance improvements to come first.

decisions.summary: The fixed cost is measured first, and each figure carries the date it was observed and its method. The tests go red before the change, the expected saving is marked GUESS, and the after-measurement waits for the first real bundles.
decisions.why: This is ordering and evidence, and it narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: On a build error holding `undefined hidden symbol`, drop only the incremental session holding each `.rcgu.o` unit the linker names and that crate's `.fingerprint/<crate>-<meta>`, under cargo's own lock, print what was dropped, and rebuild once incrementally
decisions.why: This is the task line's own remedy, 'dropping that crate's incremental session', as the block quotes it. The fingerprint drop is what makes the heal work: 449 T244 cleared sessions but not fingerprints, cargo kept the broken rlib as fresh, and the scratch copy showed a stale rlib behind an out-of-date fingerprint recompiled and linked clean (e2e.log, 8.3 s). Its reach is no wider than the directories the linker names.

decisions.summary: A link error that names no unit rebuilds once with CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; a second failure is refused as before, with the cargo text
decisions.why: A bounded fallback inside the same goal: a gate command that failed on stale link state runs on a freshly linked tool. It adds no behavior beyond one retry and keeps the existing refusal afterwards. In this path the stale incremental set is left as it is (the block's own finding is that a CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 set is separate), so goal 1's 'next incremental build links with no retry' is guaranteed only for the named-unit path. That is a limit of a fallback for unrecognised failures and no narrowing of the task.

decisions.summary: An uncompiling file is still refused with no retry (T41 kept); only the link-error text triggers a retry
decisions.why: Keeps existing, separately approved behavior that T142's line does not ask to change; the detection is limited to rust-lld's own spelling.

decisions.summary: Always-non-incremental and `lto = "off"` rejected: T95's incremental tool profile and default ThinLTO kept
decisions.why: Leaves T95's measured, GM-asked profile as it is. The alternative was measured to cost 83-116 s per rebuild of the core crates against about 5 s (time.sh, measured 2026-11-22), which works against the feature's performance purpose. Keeping an approved profile is no narrowing.

decisions.summary: Show the rust-lld lines and a line naming what was dropped, not the full link command line
decisions.why: Presentation of the refusal and the heal. It serves the defect statement in Approach item 12, where a wall of linker text is the symptom.

decisions.summary: Change only scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh, its hook test and this section; the real cache is never removed by hand; red-first test (FR-012)
decisions.why: Matches T142's line and FR-012's red-first requirement (13 FAIL lines on HEAD's launcher, then green, measured 2026-11-22).

decisions.summary: The same stale-link exposure in scripts/hooks/l7r-guard.sh (l7r_guard, same incremental tool profile, l7r_shared units that failed l7r-rust twice) and in make rust-test's dev-profile builds is deferred to T146, which lands before T98
decisions.why: The fix stops at the gate launcher although the same defect class is known in two other builds, so this is a narrowing, and it is a defect left rather than a difference. It is legitimate because the defect is not left: it is filed as T146 with a stated order (before T98, whose occupancy measurement a stalled build would skew). It also states why it is not fixed here (T142's line is the gate launcher's failure, and the guard fails open to its last good binary rather than refusing every gate command). FR-009 asks for exactly those three things: a reason, a filed id and an order. Nothing the GM asked is excepted: the request does not name this defect, and the GM's 2026-11-22 words favour filing small defects and bundling them over widening one task. One caution for T146: these two instances came from a scan of transcripts for link failures, which finds builds that FAILED, not every build exposed. T146's census should be drawn from the launchers that build with CARGO_INCREMENTAL or the tool or dev profile, for example a grep over scripts/ and the Makefiles, and not from this list.

decisions.summary: A ledger refusal (--refuse or --landing) leaves out a MODE 4 pass whose subject names a feature present here and a task ticked in neither tasks file and not among the landing's tasks; it names them on stdout. Block reviews, ticked tasks', absent features' and every other pass still refuse.
decisions.why: This is the fix the task names in its heading (a landing refused on another task's open plan-review passes) and serves the request's rework clause (refused landings, improvement 6 'smaller landing fixes'). The left-out pass is not dropped: it refuses at its own task's landing and push, where that task is in the landed set or ticked. The bundle holds the heading, not T147's task line verbatim; judged against request.md and the spec.

decisions.id: reach: the rule in the set all three refusals read
decisions.summary: The rule sits in the one owed set the first pass, the push's ledger-owed --refuse row and make land-tooling read, so all three leave another open task's plan review out.
decisions.why: Same deferral as the rule. Each left-out pass still refuses at its own task's push, because that task is ticked by then (the plan says so explicitly). Enforcement moves to the landing that can answer it and is not lost, so 385 T72's 'plan reviews written by every push route' still holds for each task's own reviews.

decisions.summary: A task id in neither tasks.md nor tasks-done.md counts as open, so its pass is left out.
decisions.why: A design detail of the fix with a stated, measured-against-history reason: land-alone commits a task's own lines only (de7ecc7de4), so another task's line can be absent at the landing worktree's HEAD. It removes no requested behavior.

decisions.summary: A feature's landing still writes every pass traced to it, another open task's plan review included, and --write-plan-reviews still writes any recorded one; 'left to that task's landing' governs refusal, not writing.
decisions.why: Measurement corrected the heading's premise ('which only that task's landing writes'). Keeping the earliest write route changes nothing asked and narrows nothing: more rows get written, none fewer.

decisions.id: no escape added at the first pass
decisions.summary: cheap.rs asks --refuse --landing <feature> --tasks <ids>; LEDGER_ROWS_OK stays at the push and make land-tooling only.
decisions.why: The heading's second half is answered by removing the refusal the landing could not answer, rather than by adding a way past it. By the plan's own defect test (checklist item 12: a landing refused that its own work could not answer), the refusals left are the other passes. Its own session clears them with the named make ledger-owed WRITE= and a commit. The '70 still owed with the clone's 46 uncommitted rows added' sentence shows they are rows the session itself has not yet written, not rows a landing cannot reach. With no wrong outcome left there is no defect left (constitution XIV v2.36.0), and adding no bypass fits the GM's 'real enforcement and not just instructions'. FR-012's escape rule covers FR-006 to 009, 011 and 013, not this ledger refusal that predates the feature.

decisions.id: found and left: the 86-133 untied passes
decisions.summary: The passes no subject ties to a feature (impl-drift DECIDE_OK dispatches, workflow units, modal and record checks) refuse every landing until the session writes and commits their rows; called working as designed, not filed.
decisions.why: Rises or falls with the escape decision, on the same reading. These are passes the landing's session ran and can write itself with the remedy the refusal names, so they are a refusal the landing's own work can answer, not a defect deferred. FR-009's deferral form is therefore not owed.

decisions.why: The GM's 2026-11-22 premise is that each task pays the same process; measuring it first is how the plan checks that premise (Principle: measured, not assumed). Every figure carries a 2026-11-22 one-shot label with its method.

decisions.summary: Bundling = make task-start, make closing-checks and make decide take T=a,b,c as make land already does; one section, one review, one verdict entered for each member, one landing
decisions.why: Directly what the GM asked: small open tasks 'bundled together and worked at the same time' instead of each going through the same process, and 'let's do that'. The landing half already existed (T06); this adds the rest.

decisions.why: Each member still passes every existing refusal (open box, phase task, held feature, parked stage, and FR-013's perf ordering by the same path), so the bundle does not open a way around them; it is the mechanism of working them at the same time.

decisions.summary: The event log files a T=a,b,c command under its first task, so FR-007's static-runs guard counts the bundle's runs once and the plan-round tripwire its rounds once; PLAN_ROUND_CAP and STATIC_RUNS_A_TASK unchanged
decisions.why: A bundle is one unit of work and gets one task's budget under each guard - no looser than a single task, so FR-007's and the 2026-11-19 'real enforcement' are not weakened; the cost paid once is the request's point.

decisions.summary: A heading opening with a task-id list followed by (bundle), Approach, part B or Performance checklist is each listed task's own; any other id list (feature 405's 15 headings) stays its first task's as before
decisions.why: Keeps existing plans' headings reading as they did, a compatibility choice, not a carve-out from bundling: any bundle written in the new form is read as each member's. It keeps no behavior the GM asked to change.

decisions.summary: make decide T=a,b,c refused while a member's section is not the first's or T= is not the heading's list; lint once, checklist per member; one MODE 4 prompt asking the reviewer to judge every task in it
decisions.why: One section and one review for the bundle is what was asked; the refusals keep a member from being reviewed by another's section, and the per-member checklist and review keep each task judged.

decisions.summary: record-task on the first task writes the same entry under each member whose section is the same; tick (owed_for) and push (judge_in) read a block in several tasks' sections as in scope where any is; the Approach gate and the plan-round count read the bundle heading
decisions.why: Each member still carries a recorded verdict before its tick and push, so feature 243's gate holds for every task; only its cost is paid once.

decisions.summary: make closing-checks T=a,b,c: the split's task is a set, the members' edit lines the caller's
decisions.why: One closing run over the bundle's files is one of the fixed costs the GM asked to pay once.

decisions.summary: No automatic chooser of which tasks are tiny; a builder or session handed tiny open tasks starts them as one, and nothing limits a bundle's size
decisions.why: The GM asked that small tasks be able to be bundled and worked together and said 'let's do that'; he did not ask for an automatic selector or a size gate. The mechanism, plus the session picking tiny open tasks as he described, is the plain reading.

decisions.summary: Task filing is not cut back or changed
decisions.why: The GM's own words: 'not bother cutting back on new tasks filed'.

decisions.summary: A single task's mark, section, prompt and verdict are written as before, existing tests unchanged
decisions.why: The request adds a bundle form; it asks nothing of the single-task flow.

decisions.summary: make where-time reports a bundle's time under its first task; the after-measurement of savings is a GUESS, to be measured on the first bundles landed
decisions.why: This narrows the 2026-11-19 per-task breakdown for bundled tasks: the other members get no time of their own. Splitting it is physically impossible: one builder, one set of closing runs and one review serve all the members at once, so there is no per-member split to measure. The bundle's whole time is still reported and none is lost, which is what the breakdown is for. Calling the savings a GUESS until measured is the project's rule, not a gap.

decisions.summary: T141 is a [perf] task under FR-013 (speeds the builders' loop), its checklist answered in those terms
decisions.why: FR-013 names 'the builders' loop' as performance work; paying the fixed cost once per bundle speeds it, and the GM asked that performance work come first.

blocks: ### T141 (each task pays the whole fixed cost whatever its fix's size - a builder, closing runs, a checklist section, `make decide`, its plan review rounds, a landing - and the GM asked that small tasks be bundled and worked at the same time, request.md "on bundling small tasks")
### T141 Approach (checklist part A)
### T141 Performance checklist (docs/performance-checklist.md - prompts, never a gate; time is the goal, calls the measure)

decisions.summary: Measure the per-task fixed cost (builders, builder and agent minutes, review rounds, closing runs, landings) over 451's 107 landed tasks before building; conclude the saving is in builder reading-in, closing runs and review rounds, the landing already multi-task (T06).
decisions.why: Serves the GM's 'every individual task goes through the same process ... feels like it is itself the issue' by measuring that process; every figure carries a date and method. One wording oddity, not a finding: 'closing runs per task median 2, 58 tasks with one' reads only if 'with one' means 'with any run'.

decisions.summary: make task-start T=a,b,c: every member's refusals checked first (not an open box, a phase task, a held feature) with nothing written while one stands; active-task names the first as task and all as tasks; each member's start logged, the first last, so it is in force and each member counts as started for land-alone (T101).
decisions.why: The GM asked that tiny open tasks be 'worked basically at the same time'; a bundle start is that. Applying each task's own refusals to every member keeps a single task's rules; refusing a phase task keeps the bundle to the small tasks the GM named.

decisions.summary: FR-013 (performance first) asked of the bundle: ruled on the reading that FR-013's refusal is one of 'every member's refusal', so a non-performance member is refused while an open performance task exists, as it would be started alone.
decisions.why: The plan's constraint names FR-013 'asked of the bundle' and its test row 'performance first'; 'every member's refusal first' carries each member's task-start refusals, FR-013's among them. On this reading the bundle cannot carry a non-performance task past the queue the GM asked for ('prioritize performance improvements'). Had FR-013 been checked on the first member only, a non-performance task could ride in under a performance first task: that would narrow FR-013 and be NOT LEGITIMATE. The builder must implement the per-member reading.

decisions.summary: The bundle is chosen by the session (a builder is 'handed' tiny open tasks), carried by T=a,b,c and the docs; no tool proposes the set or judges a task 'tiny', and nothing requires bundling.
decisions.why: The GM's words put the choosing in the session's hands: 'look at the current feature and say, hey, what set of tasks is currently open? All of which are very tiny'. Tininess is a judgment, not a mechanical property; the clause is carried by the T=a,b,c forms plus the docs step in Approach item 5. The 'real enforcement' sentence of 2026-11-19 approved the six improvements and four data ideas, not T141, and is not stretched here.

decisions.summary: The event log files a T=a,b,c command under its first task, so the static-runs guard (FR-007) and the plan-round tripwire count a bundle's runs and rounds once; STATIC_RUNS_A_TASK and PLAN_ROUND_CAP unchanged.
decisions.why: No loosening: a bundle of n tasks gets one task's allowance of make static runs and plan rounds, not n. FR-007's purpose (stop make static as the edit loop) is kept whole.

decisions.summary: FR-006 'a builder serves one task' read as one bundle: the bundle's builder serves its members, keyed to the first task (the one id readers read); the context-threshold guard and the resume refusal still apply.
decisions.why: Implied by the GM's own later words: tiny tasks 'could all be worked basically at the same time', 'bundle them together when fixing them'. One builder over a bundle is that request; separate builders per member would defeat its stated purpose (the builder's reading-in paid once). FR-006's purpose (small builder contexts) is untouched: the context threshold still refuses past it, and the bundle is restricted to tiny tasks by the GM's own framing. The plan does not name FR-006 explicitly; it should, but the reading is sound.

decisions.summary: make where-time reports a bundle's time under its first task; the other members show no time of their own.
decisions.why: FR-005 / the original request's per-task breakdown cannot be honoured member by member for a bundle: one builder's minutes, one closing run and one review round worked for all of them at once have no true split, and any allocation would be an invention rather than a measurement. The GM's bundling request itself makes the time joint. Booking it once, under the bundle's first task, is the honest measurement; it is what the retrospective should then show.

decisions.summary: plan_text::leading_tasks: a heading opening with a task-id list followed by (bundle), Approach, part B or Performance checklist is every listed task's own section; any other list heading (405's 15) stays its first task's.
decisions.why: One section for the bundle is the 'worked at the same time' request; leaving existing non-bundle list headings as they were keeps a single task's flow unchanged and is not a narrowing of anything the GM asked.

decisions.summary: make decide T=a,b,c: refused while a member's section is not the first's or T= is not the heading's list; lint once, checklist per member; one MODE 4 prompt asking the reviewer to judge every task in it.
decisions.why: One review for the bundle is the fixed cost paid once; refusals keep the bundle coherent; every member still gets its checklist and its judgment, so no task escapes review.

decisions.summary: record-task on the first writes the same verdict under each listed task with the same section; the tick (owed_for), push (judge_in), Approach gate and plan-round count read a bundle heading for each member.
decisions.why: Each member keeps its own recorded CLEAR verdict as the plan-stage gate requires; nothing ticks without one.

decisions.summary: make closing-checks T=a,b,c: its split's task a set, the members' edit lines the caller's.
decisions.why: One closing run over the bundle's files is the GM's bundling; the members' edits are all checked.

decisions.summary: A single task's mark, section, prompt and verdict are written as before; existing tests unchanged and passing; red-first tests (FR-012); budget one landing.
decisions.why: The GM asked to add bundling, not to change a single task's flow; red-first and the tests enforce the requested behavior.

decisions.summary: On a build error holding `undefined hidden symbol`, drop only the incremental session holding each `.rcgu.o` unit the linker names and that crate's `.fingerprint/<crate>-<meta>`, under cargo's own lock, print what was dropped, and rebuild once incrementally
decisions.why: This is the task line's own remedy, 'dropping that crate's incremental session', as the block quotes it. The fingerprint drop is what makes the heal work: 449 T244 cleared sessions but not fingerprints, cargo kept the broken rlib as fresh, and the scratch copy showed a stale rlib behind an out-of-date fingerprint recompiled and linked clean (e2e.log, 8.3 s). Its reach is no wider than the directories the linker names.

decisions.summary: A link error that names no unit rebuilds once with CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; a second failure is refused as before, with the cargo text
decisions.why: A bounded fallback inside the same goal: a gate command that failed on stale link state runs on a freshly linked tool. It adds no behavior beyond one retry and keeps the existing refusal afterwards. In this path the stale incremental set is left as it is (the block's own finding is that a CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 set is separate), so goal 1's 'next incremental build links with no retry' is guaranteed only for the named-unit path. That is a limit of a fallback for unrecognised failures and no narrowing of the task.

decisions.summary: An uncompiling file is still refused with no retry (T41 kept); only the link-error text triggers a retry
decisions.why: Keeps existing, separately approved behavior that T142's line does not ask to change; the detection is limited to rust-lld's own spelling.

decisions.summary: Always-non-incremental and `lto = "off"` rejected: T95's incremental tool profile and default ThinLTO kept
decisions.why: Leaves T95's measured, GM-asked profile as it is. The alternative was measured to cost 83-116 s per rebuild of the core crates against about 5 s (time.sh, measured 2026-11-22), which works against the feature's performance purpose. Keeping an approved profile is no narrowing.

decisions.summary: Show the rust-lld lines and a line naming what was dropped, not the full link command line
decisions.why: Presentation of the refusal and the heal. It serves the defect statement in Approach item 12, where a wall of linker text is the symptom.

decisions.summary: Change only scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh, its hook test and this section; the real cache is never removed by hand; red-first test (FR-012)
decisions.why: Matches T142's line and FR-012's red-first requirement (13 FAIL lines on HEAD's launcher, then green, measured 2026-11-22).

decisions.summary: The same stale-link exposure in scripts/hooks/l7r-guard.sh (l7r_guard, same incremental tool profile, l7r_shared units that failed l7r-rust twice) and in make rust-test's dev-profile builds is deferred to T146, which lands before T98
decisions.why: The fix stops at the gate launcher although the same defect class is known in two other builds, so this is a narrowing, and it is a defect left rather than a difference. It is legitimate because the defect is not left: it is filed as T146 with a stated order (before T98, whose occupancy measurement a stalled build would skew). It also states why it is not fixed here (T142's line is the gate launcher's failure, and the guard fails open to its last good binary rather than refusing every gate command). FR-009 asks for exactly those three things: a reason, a filed id and an order. Nothing the GM asked is excepted: the request does not name this defect, and the GM's 2026-11-22 words favour filing small defects and bundling them over widening one task. One caution for T146: these two instances came from a scan of transcripts for link failures, which finds builds that FAILED, not every build exposed. T146's census should be drawn from the launchers that build with CARGO_INCREMENTAL or the tool or dev profile, for example a grep over scripts/ and the Makefiles, and not from this list.

### T147 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: A ledger refusal (--refuse or --landing) leaves out a MODE 4 pass whose subject names a feature present here and a task ticked in neither tasks file and not among the landing's tasks; it names them on stdout. Block reviews, ticked tasks', absent features' and every other pass still refuse.
decisions.why: This is the fix the task names in its heading (a landing refused on another task's open plan-review passes) and serves the request's rework clause (refused landings, improvement 6 'smaller landing fixes'). The left-out pass is not dropped: it refuses at its own task's landing and push, where that task is in the landed set or ticked. The bundle holds the heading, not T147's task line verbatim; judged against request.md and the spec.

decisions.id: reach: the rule in the set all three refusals read
decisions.summary: The rule sits in the one owed set the first pass, the push's ledger-owed --refuse row and make land-tooling read, so all three leave another open task's plan review out.
decisions.why: Same deferral as the rule. Each left-out pass still refuses at its own task's push, because that task is ticked by then (the plan says so explicitly). Enforcement moves to the landing that can answer it and is not lost, so 385 T72's 'plan reviews written by every push route' still holds for each task's own reviews.

decisions.summary: A task id in neither tasks.md nor tasks-done.md counts as open, so its pass is left out.
decisions.why: A design detail of the fix with a stated, measured-against-history reason: land-alone commits a task's own lines only (de7ecc7de4), so another task's line can be absent at the landing worktree's HEAD. It removes no requested behavior.

decisions.summary: A feature's landing still writes every pass traced to it, another open task's plan review included, and --write-plan-reviews still writes any recorded one; 'left to that task's landing' governs refusal, not writing.
decisions.why: Measurement corrected the heading's premise ('which only that task's landing writes'). Keeping the earliest write route changes nothing asked and narrows nothing: more rows get written, none fewer.

decisions.id: no escape added at the first pass
decisions.summary: cheap.rs asks --refuse --landing <feature> --tasks <ids>; LEDGER_ROWS_OK stays at the push and make land-tooling only.
decisions.why: The heading's second half is answered by removing the refusal the landing could not answer, rather than by adding a way past it. By the plan's own defect test (checklist item 12: a landing refused that its own work could not answer), the refusals left are the other passes. Its own session clears them with the named make ledger-owed WRITE= and a commit. The '70 still owed with the clone's 46 uncommitted rows added' sentence shows they are rows the session itself has not yet written, not rows a landing cannot reach. With no wrong outcome left there is no defect left (constitution XIV v2.36.0), and adding no bypass fits the GM's 'real enforcement and not just instructions'. FR-012's escape rule covers FR-006 to 009, 011 and 013, not this ledger refusal that predates the feature.

decisions.id: found and left: the 86-133 untied passes
decisions.summary: The passes no subject ties to a feature (impl-drift DECIDE_OK dispatches, workflow units, modal and record checks) refuse every landing until the session writes and commits their rows; called working as designed, not filed.
decisions.why: Rises or falls with the escape decision, on the same reading. These are passes the landing's session ran and can write itself with the remedy the refusal names, so they are a refusal the landing's own work can answer, not a defect deferred. FR-009's deferral form is therefore not owed.
